studies.label: Controlled crossover experiment: public transport and university-space ideation

arms.name: ChatGPT-assisted ideation
arms.description: Supervised ideation with ChatGPT on university-provided computers; other websites and tools were restricted. Group B received this condition for the public-transport task; Group A received it for the subsequent university-spaces task. These are crossover condition labels, not separate participant samples (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).

arms.name: Unaided ideation
arms.description: Supervised ideation in a computer-free classroom without external support. Group A received this condition for the public-transport task; Group B received it for the subsequent university-spaces task after earlier ChatGPT use (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).

studies.task: Sketch and briefly describe innovative ideas to improve public transport and university spaces in fixed task order, reversing ChatGPT availability between tasks (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT, GPT-3.5
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.3.1: GPT-3.5 is identified; its release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is mentioned in the full document.

studies.shared_sample: Possible shared sample with c031, Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation: A crossover study in higher education (DOI 10.1016/j.tsc.2025.101958), as flagged in the reconciled screening form. Matching cohort descriptions, tasks, assistance orders and idea counts suggest overlap, but participant identity is unconfirmed. No c031 statistics are substituted for c201 results.

open_items: The paper gives the participating/analyzed cohort but no separately printed number randomized, allocation protocol, participant flow, exclusions or per-sequence/per-condition analysis counts (PDF p. 4, Section 4.1; PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1; PDF p. 16, Section 7).
Exact randomized assistance-comparison means, SDs, SEs, test statistics, p-values and effect sizes are absent; Figure 7 is unlabeled and its error bars are undefined (PDF pp. 9 and 11).

Participant-level aggregation, treatment of multiple ideas or ratings, exact analysis counts by outcome and any crossover/participant-dependence adjustment are not specified. Figure 7 does not establish the independent-unit basis of its error bars (PDF pp. 8-9, Sections 4.3.2-4.4; PDF p. 11).
Fluency is reported only as condition-level totals. Participant-level idea counts, means, dispersions and paired uncertainty are not printed (PDF p. 7, Table 3).

Washout and carryover handling are not reported; the later unaided task follows earlier ChatGPT use. There is no isolated comparison of unassisted exposed and unexposed participants on the same later task (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).
Potential participant overlap with c031 remains unconfirmed, as flagged by the reconciled screening form; treat independence across the two papers as unresolved.

The prior-experience table's idea counts do not match the assisted-condition corpus subtotal. The paper does not reconcile this discrepancy or give subgroup participant counts; those non-random comparisons were not extracted (PDF p. 7, Table 3; PDF p. 11, Table 4).
The release year of the named ChatGPT/GPT-3.5 tool is not stated in the paper, so ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 7, Section 4.3.1).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion was read from start through the final references; no appendix or supplement is present. Every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf, and Figures 1 and 7 were inspected directly in memory. All PDF page numbers equal the printed page numbers. This is one randomized-order crossover study, with separate records for each full-sample task contrast and the paper's combined-task contrast. Assignment was to individual students' condition order, not intact classrooms. The study country identifies the institution in Spain; participant nationality is not stated. Group sizes were not inferred from idea totals or other papers. Figure-only output ratings remain as records with null numeric effects. The numerical means, SDs and test statistics in Table 4 belong to non-random prior-experience comparisons and are excluded. Aggregate fluency counts are preserved only as verbatim table text, without converting totals into means. Neither a measured across-people diversity outcome nor an isolated after-AI contrast is reported. Data and materials are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request (PDF p. 17, Data Availability Statement); no supplementary data or other paper's estimates were used.
